title: AVP,Associate: Investment Professional SSF
description:
**Role Overview:**

We are looking for an investment professional to support the full investment lifecycle, from opportunity evaluation and transaction execution through closing. The role requires strong financial and analytical skills, the ability to understand businesses across sectors, and the judgement to evaluate both commercial upside and downside risks. The candidate should combine intellectual curiosity and attention to detail with a high-ownership, execution-oriented approach.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**A. Investment evaluation and underwriting**

•Analyse companies across sectors, including business model, industry structure, competitive positioning, management quality, unit economics, historical performance, cash-flow generation and key operating risks.

•Assess investment opportunities across structured debt and equity instruments, including return potential, downside scenarios, capital structure, security package, liquidity, repayment capacity and exit pathways.

•Build a clear investment thesis and identify the critical assumptions, risk factors, mitigants and value-creation levers relevant to each opportunity.

•Undertake primary and secondary research, sector benchmarking, peer analysis and management interactions to develop an independent point of view.

**B. Financial analysis and modelling**

•Build and review integrated financial models covering profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, debt schedules, working capital and scenario/sensitivity analysis.

•Analyse historical financial statements, quality of earnings, leverage, debt-servicing ability, covenant headroom, return outcomes and valuation under base, upside and downside cases.

•Prepare valuation analysis using relevant methodologies, including trading comparables, precedent transactions, discounted cash flow and transaction-specific return analysis.

•Ensure accuracy, consistency and auditability of model inputs, calculations and outputs.

**C. Transaction execution**

•Support or lead transactions end to end, including screening, structuring, term-sheet evaluation, due diligence, investment committee materials, documentation, closing and post-closing actions.

•Coordinate with management teams, promoters, intermediaries, lenders, co-investors and other transaction stakeholders.

•Manage workstreams involving financial, tax, legal, commercial, technical, ESG and other diligence agencies, and synthesize findings into key issues, investment implications and protections required.

•Work closely with external legal counsel on transaction documents, conditions precedent, representations and warranties, covenants, security creation, governance rights, events of default and exit provisions.

•Maintain execution trackers, resolve issues proactively and drive transactions to agreed timelines without compromising analytical rigour.

**D. Investment committee and communication**

•Prepare clear, concise and decision-oriented screening notes, investment memoranda, presentations and approval materials.

•Present analysis and recommendations to senior investment professionals and respond to questions with well-supported data and judgement.

•Identify information gaps, challenge management assumptions constructively and communicate key risks without losing sight of the overall investment case.

•
**Qualification:**
MBA/PGDM with CA preferred; exceptional candidates with strong transaction experience will also be considered. Relevant experience in private equity, private credit, structured finance, investment banking, transaction advisory, corporate finance or a comparable investing/execution role. Demonstrated experience analyzing businesses and financial performance across multiple sectors; experience should show depth of thinking rather than only process exposure

•Prior end-to-end transaction execution experience is strongly preferred, including coordination of diligence advisors and legal counsel.

·
**Experience**
: 3-6 Years; Experience in structured credit, special situations, private equity or complex/bespoke transactions will be an advantage

·
**Analytical depth:**
Breaks complex issues into their financial, commercial and legal components; tests assumptions and connects detail to the investment conclusion.

·
**Commercial judgement:**
Understands how a business makes money, what can go wrong and which risks can be priced, structured or contractually protected.

·
**Creative problem-solving:**
Thinks beyond standard templates and develops practical, transaction-specific solutions while remaining grounded in risk and return

·
**Ownership and execution:**
Takes responsibility for outcomes, follows through on commitments and remains dependable under tight and changing timelines.

·
**Attention to detail:**
Maintains accuracy and consistency across numbers, documents, diligence findings and transaction trackers

·
**Curiosity and initiative:**
Proactively seeks information, develops sector knowledge and forms an independent, evidence-based view

·
**Collaboration and maturity:**
Works effectively with senior professionals, portfolio management teams, advisors and counterparties; challenges constructively and communicates with clarity.

·
**Integrity and resilience:**
Demonstrates sound judgement, discretion, a strong work ethic and the ability to remain composed through demanding transaction situations

title: Analyst, CMBS Ratings - India
description:
About Us: Morningstar DBRS is a leading provider of independent rating services and opinions for corporate and sovereign entities, financial institutions, and structured finance instruments globally. Currently with 700 employees in eight offices globally. Formed through the July 2019 acquisition of DBRS by Morningstar, Inc., the ratings business is the fourth-largest provider of credit ratings in the world. Morningstar DBRS is committed to empowering investor success, serving the market through leading-edge technology and raising the bar for the industry. Morningstar DBRS is a market leader in Canada, the U.S. and Europe in multiple asset classes. Morningstar DBRS rates more than 4,000 issuers and 60,000 securities worldwide and is driven to bringing more clarity, diversity of opinion, and responsiveness to the ratings process. Morningstar DBRS approach and size provide the agility to respond to customers’ needs, while being large enough to provide the necessary expertise and resources. Visit: https://dbrs.morningstar.com/ to learn more.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a member of the CMBS team, you will conduct thorough quantitative and qualitative research on the underlying loans and properties that collateralize Commercial Mortgage Backed Securities transactions. In addition, you will assist the onshore team with setting up Net Cash flow models; assist with special projects/initiatives, as needed. With some seasoning, you also will be expected to have thorough understanding underwriting and support on various other task across the ratings value chain. This position is based in our Navi Mumbai office.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Analyze the credit risk in SF securities by performing tasks that includes reviewing deal documents, analyzing periodic data and setting up net cashflow templates.
* Collect, organize and analyze data from internal and external sources for use in criteria development, ratings and research reports.
* Accurate and timely retrieval, analysis, research and reporting of CMBS pool level and property level performance, including:
* Identifying and analyzing risky assets based upon qualitative and quantitative factors o Identifying macro and micro risk factors, including market, property type, tenant, and borrower, to determine and measure exposure within the CMBS pools and loan portfolios.
* Monitoring, analysis, and executive summary reporting on CMBS transactions, including an investigation of potential default or loss scenarios for underlying real estate loan collateral.
* Compile and prepare periodic portfolio reports for use by senior staff and identify material changes for research causes.
* Maintain regular and open communication with the operations team and technology team about assigned tasks, priorities and ensure applications under development meet the defined requirements and pass the user acceptance testing prior to its release.
* Take ownership of the tasks with focus on quality and accuracy of the deliverables
* Demonstrate strong learning curve and eagerness to move up the rating value chain
* Ensure compliance with regulatory and company policies and procedures.

**Requirements**

* 3 to 5 years of experience in a credit research domain, with knowledge of CMBS, experience at a rating agency is a plus.
* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Economics, Finance or Management Studies
* Masters, CFA or CFA program enrollment are a plus
* Fluent in English, with good verbal and written communication skills
* Strong attention to detail and accuracy
* Highly motivated, self-starter who is keen to learn, has a positive attitude and a strong work ethic
* Ability to manage multiple tasks at the same time and deliver results in a timely manner
* Good inter-personal skills and ability to participate/ contribute as a team player
* Experience with Intex, REIS and CBRE is a plus

Morningstar DBRS is an equal opportunity employer
  
  
**About Us**
Morningstar DBRS is a leading provider of independent rating services and opinions for corporate and sovereign entities, financial institutions, and project and structured finance instruments globally. Rating more than 4,000 issuers and 60,000 securities, it is one of the top four credit rating agencies in the world.
  
  
Morningstar DBRS empowers investor success by bringing more transparency and a much-needed diversity of opinion in the credit rating industry. Our approach and size allow us to be nimble enough to respond to customers' needs in their local markets, but large enough to provide the necessary expertise and resources they require. Market innovators choose to work with us because of our agility, tech-forward approach, and exceptional customer service.
  
  
Morningstar DBRS is the next generation of credit ratings.
  
  
If you receive and accept an offer from us, we require that personal and any related investments be disclosed confidentiality to our Compliance team (days vary by region). These investments will be reviewed to ensure they meet Code of Ethics requirements. If any conflicts of interest are identified, then you will be required to liquidate those holdings immediately. In addition, dependent on your department and location of work certain employee accounts must be held with an approved broker (for example all, U.S. employee accounts). If this applies and your account(s) are not with an approved broker, you will be required to move your holdings to an approved broker.
  
  
Morningstar's hybrid work environment gives you the opportunity to collaborate in-person each week as we've found that we're at our best when we're purposely together on a regular basis. In most of our locations, our hybrid work model is four days in-office each week. A range of other benefits are also available to enhance flexibility as needs change. No matter where you are, you'll have tools and resources to engage meaningfully with your global colleagues.

title: Financial Reporting Manager
description:
**Overview**
CACTUS is a remote-first organization and we embrace an accelerate from anywhere culture. You may choose to work from home in Mumbai; however, you will be required to travel to our Andheri East office thrice a week for business requirements, meetings, or company/team events, or on short notice as needed.
  
  
We are looking for a highly driven and accountable finance professional to join our Reporting & Compliance team. This Individual Contributor role offers end-to-end ownership of financial reporting, group consolidation, month-end close, and audit management, serving as the key point of contact for consolidation and audit activities.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a qualified Chartered Accountant (CA) with 8-10 years of post-qualification experience, preferably in an MNC or multi-entity environment. Strong expertise in Ind AS/IFRS, financial reporting, consolidation, and audit management is essential.
  
  
We are seeking someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, embraces change, and takes ownership beyond their core responsibilities. The successful candidate will be proactive, solution-oriented, and capable of independently driving complex assignments from start to finish while contributing to the continuous improvement of the finance function.
  
  
Please note that this position is accepting applications for Mumbai based candidates only.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Month-End Close: Own and drive the month-end close process, ensuring that financial transactions, provisions, accruals and reconciliations are completed accurately and within stipulated timelines.
* Financial Reporting: Lead the preparation and review of accurate and timely standalone financial statements and related financial reporting in accordance with Ind AS, IFRS and other applicable accounting requirements.
* Group Consolidation: Lead the preparation of group consolidation financials and act as the single point of contact, including collection, review and validation of financial information, intercompany eliminations, consolidation adjustments and timely reporting.
* Audit Management: Manage and coordinate statutory, internal and other financial audits, acting as the primary point of contact for auditors. This includes audit planning, coordination, responding to queries, resolving observations and ensuring timely closure.
* Internal Controls & Compliance: Develop, implement and maintain robust financial controls and ensure compliance with applicable accounting, statutory and internal requirements. Support SOX and other control-related activities, where applicable.
* Technical Accounting: Review accounting matters, financial statement disclosures and complex reporting issues, ensuring appropriate interpretation and application of Ind AS, IFRS and other relevant requirements.
* Process Improvement & Automation: Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise and automate reporting, consolidation, close and compliance processes, and drive initiatives that improve efficiency, accuracy and control.
* Stakeholder Management: Collaborate with Tax, Treasury, Legal, Operations and other cross-functional teams, while working effectively with senior management and external auditors.
* Leadership & Team Contribution: Take the lead on new and challenging assignments, provide guidance and knowledge support to team members, proactively address issues and contribute to building a high-performing finance function.

**Qualifications And Prerequisites**

* Qualified Chartered Accountant (CA) with 8-10 years of relevant post-qualification experience.
* Strong expertise in Financial Reporting, Controllership, and Month-End/Year-End Close processes.
* Hands-on experience in Revenue Recognition and Project Accounting for long-term projects.
* Proven track record in Group Consolidation and preparation/review of standalone and consolidated financial statements.
* Experience leading Statutory and Internal Audits, including serving as the primary liaison for auditors.
* Strong working knowledge of Ind AS and IFRS with practical application in complex accounting and reporting scenarios.
* Experience in MNC, global, or multi-entity environments; service industry experience is a plus.
* Solid understanding of Internal Controls, Compliance, and SOX frameworks.
* Experience with SAP, Oracle, or similar ERP systems; exposure to automation and process improvement initiatives is preferred.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project management capabilities with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results within tight timelines.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience partnering with senior leaders and external stakeholders.
* High attention to detail, strong ownership mindset, and a proactive approach to driving improvements and creating impact beyond the scope of the role.

Application Process
  
  
Before applying, please ensure you meet the role requirements listed above and have legal authorization to work in the country where this role is advertised. Our selection process typically involves an initial screening by a recruiter, a technical assessment, and two to three interview rounds. For this role, there will be 4 rounds of interviews.
  
  
**Equal Opportunity**
Our hiring practices reflect our commitment to providing equal opportunities and creating an environment where everyone can thrive, develop, and succeed. We celebrate the uniqueness of our team members and prohibit discrimination of any kind, based on race, color, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or any other protected characteristic.
  
  
**Accelerating from Anywhere**
As a remote-first organization, these are essential attributes we look for in all our candidates.
  
  

* Taking ownership of your work with minimal supervision, showing strong ability to organize, prioritize and deliver results independently.
* Documenting work that brings everyone on the same page.
* Maturity to choose between synchronous and asynchronous collaboration.
* Effectively collaborating with colleagues across different time zones by setting dedicated hours for collaboration and keeping team members updated through your MS Teams status.

**About CACTUS**
Established in 2002, Cactus Communications is a leading technology company that specializes in expert services and AI-driven products which improve how research gets funded, published, communicated, and discovered. Its flagship brand, Editage, offers a comprehensive suite of researcher solutions, including expert editing services and cutting-edge AI tools like Mind the Graph, Paperpal, and R Discovery.
  
  
Complementing its academic offerings, the company operates Cactus Life Sciences—a specialized, global medical communications brand that provides scientific strategy, medical writing, and AI-augmented "Human-Anchored AI™" solutions for top pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies.
  
  
With offices in major global hubs including Princeton, London, Lucerne, Delaware, Singapore, Beijing, Shanghai, Seoul, Tokyo, and Mumbai, and a workforce of over 3,000 global experts, CACTUS is a pioneer in workplace best practices and has been consistently recognized as a great place to work.

title: Manager, Financial Products & Partnerships, Accion Advisory
description:
**About Accion**
Accion is a global nonprofit on a mission to create a fair and inclusive economy for the 1.6 billion people who are failed by the global financial system. We develop and scale responsible digital financial solutions for small business owners, smallholder farmers, and women, so they can make informed decisions and improve their lives. Through targeted investment strategies, advisory solutions, and expert thought leadership, we work with local partners to develop and scale cheaper, more accessible, and customer-friendly financial solutions. Since 1961, Accion has helped build 299 financial service providers serving low-income clients in 77 countries, reaching over 500 million people. More at https://www.accion.org.
  
  
**About Accion Advisory**
Accion Advisory is a global team helping companies deliver innovative, affordable financial solutions for underserved customers in emerging markets. We work with local ecosystem partners, leveraging philanthropic capital and new technologies, to test, improve, and scale solutions that strengthen economic well‑being.
  
  
Our 60+ advisors deliver 30+ active projects across Africa, Asia, and the Americas, collaborating with financial service providers, fintech companies, digital platforms, and other stakeholders to demonstrate the viability of reaching end customers often considered too risky or costly to serve. Through AI- and data-driven digital transformation and embedded financial products, we drive impact across four key pillars: livelihoods, agriculture, climate, and women's economic empowerment.
  
  
**Position Summary**
Accion Advisory is seeking a Manager, Financial Products & Partnerships to expand access to credit and risk-sharing products for smallholder farmers, agricultural MSMEs, and climate-vulnerable communities across India and beyond. You will build and lead Accion's relationships with financial service providers: MFIs, fintechs, small finance banks, and NBFCs. Taking partnerships from first conversation through executed agreement and into live pilots, and shaping the financial products those partnerships deliver. The role also supports donor and commercial fundraising for Accion's climate and agricultural finance agenda.
  
  
Based in Mumbai on a hybrid basis with two days on site, this is an open-ended position reporting to the Senior Director, Global Agri & Climate Lead, Accion Advisory. You will work closely with regional delivery teams across India, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Southeast Asia.
  
  
**Position Responsibilities**
**Product Design and Development**

* Lead the design and commercial structuring of financial products for smallholder farmers and agricultural MSMEs, including risk frameworks, credit guarantees, de-risking instruments, and blended finance incentives.
* Assess market opportunity, partner viability, and product pricing using existing models and analytical inputs, working with technical specialists where detailed financial modeling is required.
* Conduct market and customer research to identify unmet needs and opportunities for product innovation across agricultural value chains.

**Capacity Building and Knowledge Sharing**

* Build legal and regulatory structuring capacity, in-house or retained, across active markets including India, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Southeast Asia.
* Represent Accion Advisory at conferences and industry forums, contribute to knowledge products and publications, and deliver training and technical assistance to staff and partners on product development and partnership approaches.

**Financial Service Provider (FSP) Partnership and Engagement**

* Identify, prioritize, and engage financial service providers: MFIs, fintechs, small finance banks, and NBFCs to pilot credit and risk-sharing products for climate-smart assets and underserved agricultural and MSME segments.
* Lead FSP partnership development end to end, from initial outreach through MoU/LoI execution, and coordinate onboarding and pilot implementation with partners.
* Maintain a structured engagement tracker and stakeholder plan across active and prospective FSP relationships, and report pipeline progress to Advisory leadership.

**Business Development and Fundraising**

* Support donor and commercial partner prospecting for climate and agricultural finance initiatives, identifying funding opportunities and potential co-funders.
* Draft concept notes and contribute to full proposals for grant and blended finance opportunities, and support scoping conversations with commercial partners as part of Accion's partner diversification strategy.

**Position Qualifications**

* Master's degree in agricultural economics, finance, business, development studies, or a related field; a Bachelor's degree with equivalent work experience will be considered.
* 10+ years of total professional experience, including 6+ years in financial services partnerships, origination, or business development, and at least 2 years at manager level or equivalent.
* Demonstrated experience taking partnerships from initial outreach through executed agreement and into implementation.
* Experience in the agriculture sector or agritech companies, with agriculture as the primary focus.
* An established network across MFIs, fintechs, small finance banks, and NBFCs in India.
* Working knowledge of credit, risk-sharing and guarantee structures, and product pricing principles.
* Ability to interpret financial models and analysis to inform commercial decisions.
* Knowledge of agricultural value chains, smallholder farmer dynamics, and the rural finance ecosystem.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
* Ability to work effectively in a cross-cultural and collaborative environment.
* Fluency in English.
* Right to work in India.

title: Operations Specialist/Associate Manager Ops
description:
**The Impact You’ll Drive**
We are looking for
*Operations Specialist*
to manage reconciliation, settlements, disputes, and banking partner operations across card and payment programs. The role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to collaborate with banking, finance, product, and technology teams to ensure seamless and compliant payment operations.
  
  
**The Hats You Will Wear**
*Reconciliation & Settlement Operations*

* Manage daily transaction reconciliations across Credit Card and UPI programs.
* Perform end-to-end reconciliation of settlements, suspense accounts, fee accounts, and operational ledgers.
* Validate settlement files, accounting entries, and transaction reports to ensure accuracy and completeness.
* Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks, mismatches, and exceptions in coordination with Product, Technology, Finance, and Banking partners.
* Support settlement and accounting operations through preparation and validation of operational files and reports.

*Dispute & Chargeback Management*

* Manage the end-to-end lifecycle of customer disputes and chargebacks across card and payment programs.
* Coordinate with partner banks, payment networks, and internal stakeholders for timely resolution.
* Track dispute volumes, ageing, recovery rates, and adherence to defined turnaround times.
* Identify recurring dispute trends and drive corrective actions.

*Banking Partner Operations*

* Act as the operational point of contact for banking and payment partners.
* Support operational reviews, reconciliation discussions, audits, and issue resolution.
* Ensure adherence to partner SLAs and drive timely closure of operational escalations.

*Controls & Compliance*

* Ensure operational processes comply with applicable RBI, NPCI, and card network guidelines.
* Maintain process documentation, audit trails, and operational controls.
* Participate in internal and external audits and support compliance requirements.
* Identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and operational efficiency.

*Reporting & Analytics*

* Prepare daily operational dashboards, reconciliation summaries, and exception reports.
* Monitor key operational metrics and provide actionable insights.
* Conduct root cause analysis for operational issues and recommend preventive measures.

**The Perfect Fit**

* 3–6 years of experience in Banking, Fintech, Payments, Card Operations, or Reconciliation functions.
* Hands-on experience in transaction reconciliation, settlements, chargebacks, or payment operations.
* Exposure to Credit Cards, UPI, Prepaid Cards, or Digital Payments ecosystems is preferred.
* Experience working with banking partners and payment networks will be an advantage.
* Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Professional qualifications such as CA Inter, CMA, or equivalent will be an added advantage.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Strong understanding of payment transaction lifecycles and settlement processes.
* Proficiency in Excel and data analysis.
* Working knowledge of SQL is preferred.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

**The Problem We’re Solving**
Financial institutions today are held back by legacy systems that are slow, rigid, and expensive to scale. Launching or evolving credit, lending, and UPI products often takes months, requires heavy engineering effort, and limits the ability to create personalized customer experiences.
  
  
At the same time, customer expectations have changed - speed, flexibility, and tailored financial products are no longer optional. Banks and fintechs need infrastructure that allows them to innovate quickly, adapt continuously, and scale without friction.
  
  
This is where we come in.
  
  
At Vegapay, we are building modern, configurable fintech infrastructure that enables banks, NBFCs, and enterprises to design, launch, and manage credit and payment programs with ease. Our platform brings together flexibility, speed, and control - helping our partners unlock new growth opportunities and deliver personalized banking experiences at scale.
  
  
**The Opportunity Ahead**

* Work on cutting-edge credit and payments infrastructure powering leading financial institutions.
* Collaborate closely with Banking, Product, Technology, and Leadership teams.
* Be part of a high-growth fintech building the future of embedded credit.

title: Credit Risk Researcher, Vice President
description:
As a Vice President in Credit Risk Research at Citi, you will conduct high-impact analysis across wholesale and retail portfolios that directly shapes how the firm identifies, measures, and manages credit exposure. This individual contributor role gives you the platform to inform senior leadership, influence governance frameworks, and apply deep credit risk expertise to decisions with firm-wide consequences. If you can translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insight, this position offers the scope and visibility to make a lasting impact.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Conduct in-depth credit risk research across wholesale and retail portfolios, producing assessments that equip senior leadership with well-informed risk decisions.
* Develop and refine credit risk measurement methodologies, keeping Citi's approach to credit risk rigorous and aligned with evolving market conditions.
* Analyze credit portfolios to identify emerging risk concentrations, trends, and vulnerabilities, translating findings into clear risk mitigation recommendations.
* Monitor counterparty and sector-level credit risk trends to maintain an accurate, current view of Citi's credit exposures.
* Produce high-quality risk assessment reports and research outputs that communicate complex findings clearly to senior stakeholders.
* Present research conclusions to senior business and risk leaders, informing strategic credit risk decisions.
* Contribute to the development and refinement of credit risk governance frameworks, embedding research outputs into risk oversight processes.

**Required Qualifications & Skills**

* Hold a bachelor's degree in economics, finance, statistics, or a related quantitative field.
* Bring 8+ years of experience in financial services and analytics, with deep expertise in wholesale or retail credit risk research or a closely related discipline.
* Apply strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills to develop and enhance credit risk measurement methodologies.
* Interpret complex credit data to identify material risk themes and draw well-reasoned conclusions.
* Communicate nuanced credit risk findings clearly and confidently to senior and executive-level audiences, in writing and in person.
* Maintain familiarity with credit risk governance frameworks and the regulatory environment governing credit risk management in banking.
* Manage multiple research workstreams simultaneously, delivering rigorous, high-quality outputs within defined timelines.

**Beneficial Skills & Qualifications**

* Hold an advanced degree, such as a Master's, in economics, finance, statistics, or a related quantitative field.

What We Offer
  
  
At Citi, Credit Risk Research Vice Presidents work at the center of one of the world's most significant financial institutions, with direct access to complex, high-stakes analysis and the leadership teams who act on it.
  
  

* Work in a hybrid model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely, balancing structure with flexibility.
* Gain direct exposure to senior risk and business leadership, with your research informing decisions at the highest levels of the firm.
* Influence credit risk governance frameworks that shape Citi's wholesale and retail portfolio strategy.
* Build your career through Citi's global network of risk professionals and ongoing learning opportunities in credit risk.
* Thrive in a performance-driven environment that recognizes intellectual contribution, accountability, and high-quality analytical work.
* Access comprehensive wellbeing support and resources designed to support work-life balance.

Join Citi as a Vice President in Credit Risk Research and apply your expertise where it shapes the credit risk intelligence guiding one of the world's leading financial institutions.

title: Finance Executive
description:
**About Trade Bridge Advisors LLP**

Trade Bridge Advisors LLP is a Mumbai-based regulatory and trade advisory firm. Our team includes former Senior Officers of the Indian Revenue Service, who bring decades of experience in administering Customs and GST laws, along with a young, execution-focused team.

We advise on EXIM, Customs, GST, DGFT, SEZ and FEMA matters for clients across gems and jewellery, EOU / SEZ manufacturing, logistics, chemicals and engineering. As the practice grows, we are expanding the team with professionals who want to build a serious career in trade and indirect tax regulation.

**Role Overview**

This role is for a finance-trained professional who wants to build a specialised career in foreign exchange, GST and trade-linked finance. The Executive will support partners and senior consultants on FEMA, GST and financial matters for the firm's clients, including Customs, SEZ and EOU units, exporters and importers.

The role combines analytical work (reconciliations, working papers, computations) with regulatory work (returns, filings and responses to departmental queries). It suits someone who is detail-oriented, comfortable with numbers and keen to learn how finance and trade regulation intersect.

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. FEMA Support**

●      Assist in FEMA compliance for clients - export / import realisation and payment tracking, EDPMS / IDPMS follow-up and AD bank correspondence.

●      Support the preparation of filings and reporting such as FLA returns, FC-GPR / FC-TRS, ECB, ODI and related RBI / AD bank submissions.

●      Prepare working papers and draft submissions for compounding, regularisation and responses to queries from AD banks and RBI.

●      Track FEMA circulars, master directions and notifications and brief the team on changes.

**B. GST Compliance & Reconciliation**

●      Prepare and review GST returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and annual return) and reconcile with books, GSTR-2B and e-invoice / e-way bill data.

●      Work on refund claims, including exports and SEZ supplies, LUT / bond compliance and ITC analysis, with supporting working papers.

●      Assist in preparing replies to GST notices, Appeals, DRC forms and information requests from the department, with accurate data support.

**C. Finance & Certification Support**

●      Analyse client financial statements, ledgers and trial balances; prepare computations for SEZ / EOU net foreign exchange (NFE), export obligation and similar regulatory requirements.

●      Assist in drafting CA certificates, net worth and solvency statements, and financial data required for regulatory applications such as AEO, LOA and bond / licence matters.

●      Maintain organised MIS, trackers and compliance calendars for assigned clients.

**D. Client Coordination**

●      Coordinate with client accounts teams to obtain data, resolve mismatches and meet statutory deadlines.

●      Support partners in preparing client presentations, notes and responses on finance and compliance queries.

**Qualifications & Experience**

**Educational Qualification**

●      CA Intern (Inter-qualified), CA Final qualified or qualified CA.

●      B.Com / M.Com with strong accounting fundamentals will also be considered along with CA Inter.

**Work Experience**

●      Minimum 3 years of experience (articleship and post-qualification work combined) in a CA firm or consultancy, with GST, FEMA, international taxation or audit exposure.

●      Demonstrated hands-on handling of GST returns, reconciliations or FEMA / RBI filings, with a genuine interest in trade and foreign exchange regulation.

**Skills & Knowledge**

●      Working knowledge of GST law and returns; basic understanding of FEMA and RBI regulations (or strong willingness to learn).

●      Good command of Excel (lookups, pivots, reconciliations) and familiarity with Tally or similar accounting software.

●      Familiarity with the GST Portal, RBI / AD bank portals or the ability to learn quickly.

●      Clear written communication for working papers, emails and draft submissions.

**Personal Attributes**

●      Strong attention to detail, accuracy and a disciplined approach to deadlines.

●      Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to learn from senior professionals.

●      Integrity and strict confidentiality in handling client financial data.

**What We Offer**

●      Rare exposure to FEMA and trade-linked finance alongside GST - a niche, in-demand skill set for a CA career.

●      A knowledge-intensive environment with exposure to varied mandates across industries and regulators.

●      Direct access to and mentorship from senior partners, including retired senior officers of the Indian Revenue Service.

●      Genuine scope for growth, with responsibility increasing as capability is demonstrated.

●      Competitive remuneration commensurate with experience and aligned to consultancy market standards.

**How to Apply**

**Job Description**
Counterparty Credit Risk and Portfolio Management (CCRPM) team within GMFR is responsible for managing counterparty concentration, performing counterparty portfolio analysis and delivering the BAU counterparty stress testing. Additionally, the analyst will assist in the managing of counterparty concentration limits at the counterparty level across asset classes. title: Senior Manager / Manager - Cost Accountant (Mining Operations)
description:
**Department**

Finance & Accounts — Costing & MIS

**Reporting to**

Chief Financial Officer (through Head – Costing & MIS, where applicable)

**Location**

Corporate Office, Mumbai, with regular travel to Indian project sites and periodic international travel

**Experience**

6–10 years post-qualification, of which at least 3 years in mining, earthmoving, construction or heavy-equipment-intensive operations

**Qualification**

CMA (ICMAI) — preferred; CA with strong costing exposure also considered

**ABOUT TEIPL**

Thriveni Earthmovers & Infra Private Limited (TEIPL), a subsidiary of Lloyds Metals and Energy Limited, is one of India’s leading Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) companies, providing end-to-end mining solutions for iron ore, coal, barytes, copper, manganese and gold. TEIPL also manages iron ore slurry pipelines and pellet manufacturing.

TEIPL operates a fleet of more than 6,000 heavy mining equipment — including excavators, dumpers, dozers, graders, drills and support equipment — across project sites in four states in India, with international operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Papua New Guinea (PNG) and Indonesia. Its strengths lie in operational scale, in-house rebuilding of heavy equipment at its large workshops, innovation, sustainability and community engagement.

**ROLE PURPOSE**

The Cost Accountant will own the detailed cost analysis of TEIPL’s mining operations, with a primary focus on three cost pools: equipment operating cost, manpower cost and overheads. The role converts operational and SAP data into reliable unit costs (per equipment hour, per tonne and per BCM), explains variances against budget and contract rates, and gives management and project heads clear, decision-ready insight on fleet economics, site profitability and cost reduction.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Equipment Costing (Fleet of 6,000+ Units)**

* Build and maintain equipment-wise and model-wise cost sheets covering fuel (HSD), lubricants, tyres, spares, repairs and maintenance, component overhauls, operator cost, insurance and depreciation.
* Compute Owning and Operating Cost (O&O) per machine hour and per tonne / BCM, and benchmark across sites, OEMs, equipment age and capacity classes.
* Track equipment utilisation, availability, breakdown hours and idle time, and quantify their cost impact on project margins.
* Analyse fuel consumption norms (litres per hour / per BCM) and tyre cost per hour; flag abnormal consumption by machine, site and shift.
* Evaluate repair-versus-replace, rebuild-versus-new and own-versus-hire decisions, including workshop rebuild economics and lifecycle cost analysis.
* Support costing of equipment mobilisation and relocation between sites and across countries.

**2. Manpower Costing**

* Build site-wise and function-wise manpower cost models covering on-roll employees, contract labour, operators, maintenance crew and staff, including statutory costs (PF, ESI, bonus, gratuity) and benefits.
* Analyse overtime, shift allowances, camp and accommodation costs, and manpower productivity (cost per operator hour, tonnes / BCM per employee).
* Monitor actual headcount and cost against approved manning norms and budgets; highlight excess deployment and overtime drivers.
* Model the cost of expatriate and local manpower for international projects, including allowances, travel and local statutory costs.

**3. Overhead Analysis and Allocation**

* Classify site overheads (camp, security, power, administration, HSE, IT) and corporate / regional overheads; design and maintain logical, auditable allocation bases.
* Allocate overheads to projects, cost centres and profit centres to arrive at true project-level profitability.
* Identify fixed versus variable behaviour of overheads and their sensitivity to volume changes.

**4. Project / Site Profitability and Contract Costing**

* Prepare monthly project-wise cost and profitability statements, with variance analysis split into volume and rate effects against budget and prior periods.
* Test unit costs per tonne / BCM; give favourable variances the same scrutiny as adverse ones.
* Support MDO and contract-mining rate build-ups, bid costing for new tenders, escalation and price-variation claims, and rate-justification workings for customers.
* Prepare budgets, forecasts and rolling estimates of cost at site and consolidated level.

**5. International Operations (DRC, PNG, Indonesia)**

* Extend the costing framework to overseas entities, ensuring consistent cost structures, currency treatment and comparability with India operations.
* Support cost data required for inter-company charges and transfer pricing documentation.

**6. Systems, MIS and Analytics**

* Use SAP S/4HANA (CO, CO-PA, PM and MM modules) for cost-centre, internal-order and equipment-wise cost capture; drive master-data hygiene and correct cost postings at source.
* Design dashboards and MIS on equipment cost, manpower cost and overheads using advanced Excel and Power BI (or similar tools).
* Prepare monthly cost reports and presentations for the CFO, MD and project heads, with clear commentary and recommended actions.

**7. Cost Records, Cost Audit and Controls**

* Maintain cost records under the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014 and ensure compliance with applicable Cost Accounting Standards (CAS).
* Coordinate with cost auditors and statutory auditors; prepare cost audit schedules, reconciliations of cost and financial records, and supporting documentation.
* Conduct physical verification, reconciliation and valuation reviews for fuel, spares, tyres and stores at sites.
* Strengthen internal controls over cost booking, consumption approvals and equipment cost capture, in line with IPO-readiness requirements.

**8. Cost Reduction and Business Partnering**

* Partner with operations, maintenance (P&M), procurement and HR to identify and quantify cost-saving opportunities.
* Track the realisation of cost-reduction initiatives and report savings achieved against targets.

**CANDIDATE PROFILE**

**Must-have**

* CMA qualification (or CA with demonstrable costing depth).
* 6–10 years of costing experience, with at least 3 years in mining, earthmoving, infrastructure / EPC, construction equipment or a similar asset-heavy operation.
* Hands-on experience of equipment-wise costing: cost per hour, fuel and tyre norms, maintenance cost and utilisation analysis.
* Strong grounding in manpower cost modelling and overhead allocation.
* Working knowledge of SAP (CO / CO-PA; PM exposure preferred) and advanced Excel.
* Experience handling cost audit and maintaining cost records under the Companies Act.

**Good-to-have**

* Exposure to MDO / contract-mining rate build-ups, bid costing or escalation claims.
* Experience with multi-site or multi-country operations, including Africa or South-East Asia.
* Power BI, SQL or similar analytics tools.
* Exposure to IPO-readiness, internal financial controls (IFC) or listed-company reporting.

**Behavioural competencies**

* Analytical rigour and an eye for detail, with the ability to present conclusions simply to non-finance managers.
* Willingness to travel to remote mine sites in India and abroad.
* Integrity, ownership and the ability to challenge operational data constructively.

**KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

**Timeliness**

Monthly equipment, manpower and project cost reports issued within agreed close timelines

**Accuracy**

Reconciliation of cost records with financial books; minimal audit observations

**Insight**

Variances explained in volume and rate terms for all material cost heads

**Cost reduction**

Savings identified and realised against annual targets

**Compliance**

Timely cost audit closure and filing; CAS compliance

**Systems**

Improvement in SAP equipment-wise cost capture and master-data quality

title: Associate - SSF Investment Professional
description: Role Overview:We are looking for an investment professional to support the full investment lifecycle, from opportunity evaluation and transaction execution through closing. The role requires strong financial and analytical skills, the ability to understand businesses across sectors, and the judgement to evaluate both commercial upside and downside risks. The candidate should combine intellectual curiosity and attention to detail with a high-ownership, execution-oriented approach.Key Responsibilities:A. Investment evaluation and underwriting•Analyse companies across sectors, including business model, industry structure, competitive positioning, management quality, unit economics, historical performance, cash-flow generation and key operating risks.•Assess investment opportunities across structured debt and equity instruments, including return potential, downside scenarios, capital structure, security package, liquidity, repayment capacity and exit pathways.•Build a clear investment thesis and identify the critical assumptions, risk factors, mitigants and value-creation levers relevant to each opportunity.•Undertake primary and secondary research, sector benchmarking, peer analysis and management interactions to develop an independent point of view.B. Financial analysis and modelling•Build and review integrated financial models covering profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, debt schedules, working capital and scenario/sensitivity analysis.•Analyse historical financial statements, quality of earnings, leverage, debt-servicing ability, covenant headroom, return outcomes and valuation under base, upside and downside cases.•Prepare valuation analysis using relevant methodologies, including trading comparables, precedent transactions, discounted cash flow and transaction-specific return analysis.•Ensure accuracy, consistency and auditability of model inputs, calculations and outputs.C. Transaction execution•Support or lead transactions end to end, including screening, structuring, term-sheet evaluation, due diligence, investment committee materials, documentation, closing and post-closing actions.•Coordinate with management teams, promoters, intermediaries, lenders, co-investors and other transaction stakeholders.•Manage workstreams involving financial, tax, legal, commercial, technical, ESG and other diligence agencies, and synthesize findings into key issues, investment implications and protections required.•Work closely with external legal counsel on transaction documents, conditions precedent, representations and warranties, covenants, security creation, governance rights, events of default and exit provisions.•Maintain execution trackers, resolve issues proactively and drive transactions to agreed timelines without compromising analytical rigour.D. Investment committee and communication•Prepare clear, concise and decision-oriented screening notes, investment memoranda, presentations and approval materials.•Present analysis and recommendations to senior investment professionals and respond to questions with well-supported data and judgement.•Identify information gaps, challenge management assumptions constructively and communicate key risks without losing sight of the overall investment case.•Qualification: MBA/PGDM with CA preferred; exceptional candidates with strong transaction experience will also be considered. Relevant experience in private equity, private credit, structured finance, investment banking, transaction advisory, corporate finance or a comparable investing/execution role. Demonstrated experience analyzing businesses and financial performance across multiple sectors; experience should show depth of thinking rather than only process exposure•Prior end-to-end transaction execution experience is strongly preferred, including coordination of diligence advisors and legal counsel.·Experience: 3-6 Years; Experience in structured credit, special situations, private equity or complex/bespoke transactions will be an advantage·Analytical depth: Breaks complex issues into their financial, commercial and legal components; tests assumptions and connects detail to the investment conclusion.·Commercial judgement: Understands how a business makes money, what can go wrong and which risks can be priced, structured or contractually protected.·Creative problem-solving: Thinks beyond standard templates and develops practical, transaction-specific solutions while remaining grounded in risk and return·Ownership and execution: Takes responsibility for outcomes, follows through on commitments and remains dependable under tight and changing timelines.·Attention to detail: Maintains accuracy and consistency across numbers, documents, diligence findings and transaction trackers·Curiosity and initiative: Proactively seeks information, develops sector knowledge and forms an independent, evidence-based view·Collaboration and maturity: Works effectively with senior professionals, portfolio management teams, advisors and counterparties; challenges constructively and communicates with clarity.·Integrity and resilience: Demonstrates sound judgement, discretion, a strong work ethic and the ability to remain composed through demanding transaction situations

title: Senior Associate Valuations Control
description:
SS&C is a leading provider of mission-critical, AI-powered technology and services empowering financial services and healthcare organizations to work smarter, faster, and securely. Founded in 1986, SS&C is headquartered in Windsor, Connecticut, and has offices worldwide. More than 23,000 financial services and healthcare organizations, from the world's largest companies to small and mid-market firms, rely on SS&C for expertise, scale, and technology.
  
  
**Job Description**
Job Summary:\*\*
  
  
The Senior Associate Valuations Control will play a crucial role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of valuations for a variety of financial instruments. This position involves performing independent price verification, reconciling valuations, and supporting the overall valuation control framework.
  
  
Job Responsibilities:\*\*
  
  

* Perform independent price verification (IPV) on a diverse range of financial instruments, including but not limited to fixed income, equities, derivatives, and alternative investments.
* Reconcile internal valuations with external pricing sources and identify, investigate, and resolve discrepancies.
* Ensure adherence to established valuation policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
* Prepare detailed valuation reports and documentation for internal and external stakeholders, including auditors and clients.
* Collaborate with front office, risk management, and operations teams to understand and address valuation-related issues.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of valuation methodologies, systems, and controls.
* Assist in the development and implementation of new valuation models and processes.
* Participate in special projects and ad-hoc analysis as required by management.
* Provide training and mentorship to junior team members, fostering a culture of continuous learning and development.

Job Qualifications:\*\*
  
  

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field. Master's degree or professional certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM) are highly desirable.
* 4-7 years of experience in valuation control, product control, or a similar role within the financial services industry, preferably with exposure to a variety of asset classes.
* Strong understanding of financial instruments, valuation techniques, and market conventions.
* Proficiency in financial modeling and strong analytical skills with meticulous attention to detail.
* Advanced Excel skills are essential; experience with VBA, SQL, Python, or other programming languages is a plus.
* Familiarity with financial data providers (e.g., Bloomberg, Refinitiv) and valuation systems.
* Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, manage multiple priorities, and meet tight deadlines.
* A proactive and inquisitive mindset, with a strong commitment to accuracy and data integrity

Unless explicitly requested or approached by SS&C Technologies, Inc. or any of its affiliated companies, the company will not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.
  
  
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

description:
**About BII**

**British International Investment (BII)**
is the UK’s leading development finance institution, wholly owned by the UK Government. Our primary mission is to address global development challenges through strategic investments that promote sustainable and inclusive economic growth.

BII focuses on catalysing economic development, creating jobs, and building resilient economies in some of the world's most complex and underserved markets. We invest in businesses and projects that prioritise inclusive development, environmental sustainability, and innovation.

Our approach is characterised by rigorous investment standards, high governance principles, and a commitment to delivering measurable development impact. Our team consists of highly skilled and passionate professionals dedicated to making a tangible difference globally.

We foster a collaborative and intellectually stimulating work environment that values curiosity, innovation, and professional growth. Our culture balances high performance with a strong emphasis on wellbeing, ensuring our employees can achieve their full potential while contributing to our mission.

**Over 75 years**
supporting sustainable business growth in developing and emerging markets

**More than £9.9 billion**
in net assets

**1,600+**
businesses invested in

**950,000+**
workers in the businesses we support

**650+**
people in our diverse global team

**3 key development objectives: Productive | Sustainable | Inclusive**

**Team and role overview**

BII’s Asia Infrastructure – British Climate Partners is part of the Infrastructure & Climate Group. The Group focuses on making equity and mezzanine in sub sectors in infrastructure such as renewable energy, power transmission and distribution and EV mobility across India and South-East Asia.

There are 5 job levels – Associate, Executive, Manager, Director & Team Head. However, the team is very flat and people at all levels are involved in the real detail, and in representational work, both to Investment Committee and externally.

**Responsibilities**

Evaluation of new investment proposals:

* Assessing investment proposals for deals that fit within BII’s developmental and investment mandate.
* Analysing financial information relating to specific companies.
* Building or analysing financial models and conducting sensitivity analysis.
* Assisting with reports to be presented to investment committee for approval and participating in the meetings.
* Conducting detailed valuations on companies using various methods.
* Assisting with the due diligence on a specific company, sector, and country.

Portfolio Monitoring:

* Preparing periodic reports and working with the deal teams to help in the monitoring of investees financial and strategic performance

Research:

* Undertaking research into regions, countries, and specific sectors on an ad-hoc basis. This will include providing support to sector mapping exercises.
* Undertaking research relating to specific businesses or projects including traveling to meet management teams and advisers.
* Keeping up to date with market developments and monitoring factors that can affect the markets and considering how these might affect the pipeline and portfolio companies.
* Monitoring the financial news and updating the team of material information in the target countries, sector and companies.

**The Candidate**

**Background**

* Successful candidates will have relevant prior foundational work experience such as graduate programme within investment banking, consulting, private equity or credit funds in the infrastructure space, and strong solid grounding in fundamental financial modelling, excel, analytical and research skills and experience in valuation.
* Exposure to emerging market finance, especially in India is a plus
* Financial analysis skills and ability to analyse a company’s financial statements and make commercial assessments;
* Ability to work on multiple projects across products and sectors while working to deadlines and managing time effectively;
* Good business communication and presentation skills;
* Evidence of relationship building and ability to develop a network of relevant external contacts, as well as internally across different teams;
* As a member of a small team, a flexible and “hands on” approach is a prerequisite;
* Candidates should be strongly motivated by BII’s development mission and ideally demonstrate some commitment to development or social goals through previous executive or non-executive activity.

**Our cultural values**

We look for team members who aspire, as we do, to work at our best and to be:

* Impact-led, commercially rigorous
* Tenacious in the face of challenges
* Collaborative and caring

Working closely with stakeholders across Risk, Control Management, Product, Technology, Audit, and Compliance, you will help identify and address emerging risks, strengthen control practices, and support adherence to firmwide policies and regulatory expectations. * Experience with Risk and Control Assessments, issue management, control evaluation, testing, or related risk management activities.

title: Manager – Reporting
description:
**About The Role**
We are looking for a finance professional to join our Finance team as Manager – Reporting. This is primarily a financial reporting role built around five core pillars: financial reporting, deep technical knowledge of Ind AS and accounting, driving month-end close, getting statutory and internal audits fully done and closed, and owning inventory accounting. The role also requires a good understanding of how both our online (e-commerce) and offline (retail/store) businesses operate and get reflected in the numbers.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead month-end close activities end-to-end — closing calendar, accruals, provisions, and schedules — ensuring books are closed accurately and within timelines.
* Apply deep, hands-on knowledge of Ind AS and accounting standards to ensure financial statements are technically accurate and fully compliant.
* Get statutory, internal, and tax audits fully done — audit planning, PBC schedules, query resolution, and final closure — with no open items, including handling Big 4 auditors directly.
* Own inventory accounting — stock valuation, GL-to-warehouse/SCM reconciliation, obsolescence and slow-moving provisioning, and costing method reviews — as a core, ongoing responsibility.
* Build a strong working understanding of both the online (e-commerce) and offline (retail/store) sides of the business, and ensure reporting reflects channel-specific nuances (COD, returns, offline retail, store-level P&L, etc.).
* Perform variance analysis (actuals vs. budget vs. prior period) across online and offline channels and provide clear, actionable commentary to leadership.
* Coordinate with cross-functional and channel teams (online category, offline retail/stores, supply chain) to ensure reporting reflects business realities accurately.
* Support budgeting, forecasting, and board/investor reporting requirements as needed.
* Identify opportunities to automate and streamline reporting processes, dashboards, and reconciliations.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* CA with 4–6 years of post-qualification experience, primarily in financial reporting.
* Deep, hands-on knowledge of Ind AS and accounting standards — this is a core requirement, not a nice-to-have.
* Proven, hands-on experience running month-end close and independently getting statutory/internal audits fully closed.
* Experience handling Big 4 auditors, including managing the audit relationship end-to-end.
* Hands-on experience in inventory accounting — valuation, reconciliation, and provisioning — is required, not just preferred.
* Experience in a business with both online and offline (omnichannel) revenue streams — e-commerce, retail, or D2C — is strongly preferred.
* Experience with SAP HANA is preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and reporting/visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
* Exposure to IPO readiness / IPO process will be an added advantage.

**What We Are Looking For**

* A highly motivated finance professional with strong technical accounting and reporting knowledge.
* Detail-oriented with exceptional analytical and organizational skills.
* Ability to independently manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy.
* A collaborative team player with a continuous improvement mindset.
* Someone who thrives in a dynamic, high-growth environment and takes ownership of deliverables.

**Key Skills**

* Financial Reporting (Core)
* Inventory Accounting (Core)
* Ind AS & Technical Accounting
* Online & Offline Business Acumen
* Month-End Close Management
* MIS & Management Dashboards
* Statutory Audit Closure
* Reconciliations & Book Closure
* Big 4 Auditor Handling
* Internal Controls & Compliance
* Variance Analysis

title: Team Member Credit Risk Modelling
description:
**Job Summary**
Team Member – Credit Risk Modelling will be responsible for the development, enhancement, implementation, and monitoring of Internal Rating Models and Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models under IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 frameworks for wholesale portfolios. The role requires strong expertise in credit risk analytics, statistical modelling, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder management within a banking or NBFC environment.
  
  
The candidate should possess 7–8 years of relevant experience in credit risk modelling, with hands-on exposure to Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), Exposure at Default (EAD), scorecards, internal rating frameworks, and ECL implementation.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
***IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 ECL Modelling & Implementation***
Support development and maintenance of Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models under IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 framework.
  
  
Implement staging assessment methodologies, macroeconomic overlays, SICR frameworks, and forward-looking adjustments.
  
  
Monitor model performance and recommend enhancements based on portfolio behavior and economic trends.
  
  
Collaborate with finance, risk, and business teams for smooth implementation of ECL methodologies within the Bank/NBFC systems.
  
  
Support provisioning calculations, management reporting, and audit/regulatory requirements.
  
  
***Data Management & Analytics***
Perform data extraction, cleansing, transformation, and analysis using large datasets from multiple source systems.
  
  
Analyse portfolio trends, credit behaviour, migration patterns, and default characteristics.
  
  
Conduct statistical analysis and model diagnostics using SAS, SQL, Python, R, or similar analytical tools.
  
  
Prepare dashboards and analytical reports for senior management and risk committees.
  
  
***Regulatory & Governance Support***
Ensure compliance with RBI guidelines, Basel framework, IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 standards, and internal model governance policies.
  
  
Prepare model documentation, methodology papers, validation support documents, and regulatory submissions.
  
  
Support internal audit, model risk management, and regulatory inspection requirements.
  
  
***Stakeholder Management***
Work closely with Risk, Finance, Business, IT, and Model Validation teams for implementation and monitoring activities.
  
  
Present model methodologies, assumptions, and performance outcomes to senior stakeholders and committees.
  
  
Coordinate with cross-functional teams to ensure timely execution of model-related initiatives.
  
  
**Required Skills & Qualifications**
7–8 years of experience in Credit Risk Modelling within a Bank or NBFC.
  
  
Strong understanding of Internal Rating Models, Basel regulations, and IFRS 9 / Ind AS 109 ECL framework.
  
  
Hands-on experience in development/implementation of PD, LGD, EAD, scorecards, or rating models.
  
  
Good understanding of staging assessment, SICR, macroeconomic overlays, and provisioning methodologies.
  
  
Strong analytical and statistical modelling skills.
  
  
Proficiency in SAS, SQL, Python, R, or similar analytical tools.
  
  
Experience in handling large datasets and performing quantitative analysis.
  
  
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  
  
Ability to independently manage projects and interact with senior management.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**
MBA / CA / FRM / CFA / Master’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Finance, or related quantitative discipline.
  
  
Experience in model validation or regulatory interaction will be an added advantage.
  
  
Exposure to wholesale and retail credit risk portfolios preferred. Role: Assistant Vice President (AVP) – Credit Risk Modelling / IFRS 9 & Internal Rating Models

title: Presales Director-Trade Finance
description:
**Job Description**

Position Vice President – Trade Finance Solutions

Experience 10–15 years

Grade- VP Location Mumbai

Project-Fuel

**Mandatory**
-MBA-Tier 1

About FuEL

FuEL is Intellect's Flagship program designed to develop the next generation of transformation leaders for the global Fintech/Insuretech industry. Created for high-potential professionals, the program equips participants to help financial institutions reimagine business models, accelerate digital and AI transformation, and deliver exceptional customer experiences.

**The Opportunity**

This role is for a Trade Finance leader who combines deep domain expertise with hands-on technology and process experience. You will shape solution propositions for banks, actively demonstrate Intellect’s Trade Finance capabilities, and work closely with Engineering and Delivery to evolve the solution in response to market needs and client requirements. The role spans consultative engagement, product solutioning, sales support, and ongoing product

development—not just domain advisory or relationship management.

You will engage business, product, operations, and technology leaders to understand their objectives, diagnose process and business challenges, and translate them into practical, differentiated solutions. You should be equally comfortable leading a client workshop, running a product demonstration, developing a solution approach, and working with internal teams on the changes needed to deliver it.

**Role Definition**

The Vice President – Trade Finance Solutions owns domain-led solutioning and supports growth across Intellect’s Trade Finance portfolio. The role combines customer discovery, process analysis and reengineering, product demonstrations, solution design, bid support, and collaboration with Product, Engineering and Delivery to ensure that proposed solutions are credible, differentiated, feasible, and aligned with customer needs.

**Key Responsibilities**

● 1. Prospect Understanding and Process Reengineering: Engage bank and financial-institution executives, business heads, product owners, operations and technology leaders to understand business models, workflows, pain points and strategic priorities. Analyse existing processes and identify opportunities for simplification, automation, control improvement and business transformation.

● 2. Domain Expertise and Solutioning: Apply strong Trade Finance knowledge to translate business requirements

into practical solution propositions. Map customer processes and requirements to product capabilities, identify

gaps, distinguish standard product functionality from client-specific changes, and define appropriate solution options, assumptions and dependencies.

● 3. Product Demonstrations and Client Workshops: Personally lead high-quality demonstrations of Intellect’s Trade

Finance solution across the trade lifecycle, solution walkthroughs, discovery workshops, use-case discussions, proof-of-concept sessions and technical/business presentations. Tailor demonstrations to the prospect’s requirements and articulate business value, product capabilities and competitive differentiation.

● 4. Solution Design and Proposal Development: Develop customer-specific solution approaches, scope documents, functional solution notes, implementation considerations, effort-estimation inputs, assumptions, exclusions and proposal content. Ensure that proposed solutions are commercially sound, implementable and aligned with the client’s objectives.

● 5. RFP/RFI and Deal Support: Lead or contribute to RFPs, RFIs, questionnaires, bid responses and presentations. Work with Sales and Pre-sales teams to qualify opportunities, articulate value propositions, address objections and support deal progression and closure.

● 6. Product and Engineering Collaboration: Work hands-on with Product, Business Analysts, Engineering, Architecture and QA teams to assess requirements, clarify business rules, prioritize enhancements and guide solution changes. Participate in solution reviews and relevant agile ceremonies; help ensure that requirements and acceptance criteria are clear and that changes address the underlying business need.

● 7. Delivery and Implementation Collaboration: Partner with Delivery, Implementation and Support teams to validate feasibility, integrations, dependencies, customization needs, effort assumptions and delivery risks. Support transition from sales to delivery and help resolve domain or solution issues during implementation where required.

● 8. Market and Customer Feedback Loop: Capture feedback from prospects, clients, demonstrations, implementations and competitive situations. Convert insights into actionable recommendations for product enhancements, roadmap priorities, solution assets and market positioning.

● 9. Commercial and Market Development: Support new sales, cross-sell and upsell across new and existing accounts. Engage senior stakeholders, contribute to pipeline development, and build trusted-advisor relationships

by connecting domain knowledge and technology capabilities to measurable business outcomes.

● 10. Sales Enablement and Knowledge Management: Develop and maintain reusable demo flows, solution notes, product collateral, proposal content, case studies, FAQs and competitive insights. Enable Sales, Pre-sales,

Product and Delivery teams through knowledge sharing and product training.

● 11. Innovation and Industry Awareness: Track market, regulatory and technology developments relevant to Trade Finance, including opportunities to apply AI and automation. Recommend practical enhancements and differentiated capabilities based on client needs and competitive trends.

**Experience and Qualifications**

● Extensive experience in Trade Finance, with a strong track record in one or more of technology development, technology sales, pre-sales/solution consulting, product consulting, business analysis, process transformation or implementation roles. Domain knowledge alone, without meaningful process or technology solutioning experience, is not sufficient.

● Deep working knowledge of Letters of Credit, Guarantees, Documentary Collections, Open Account, trade loans/financing, amendments, limits, document handling, settlement and reporting, plus relevant SWIFT/ICC and regulatory requirements, with the ability to understand end-to-end business processes, operating models, controls, products and client-specific requirements.

● Demonstrated experience in process analysis, reengineering or transformation, and translating business challenges into functional/technology solutions for banks or financial institutions.

● Proven ability to personally conduct product demonstrations, lead customer discovery and workshops, explain solution design, and respond confidently to business and technology questions from senior stakeholders.

● Experience working directly with Product, Engineering, Architecture and Delivery teams to define requirements, evaluate feasibility, shape enhancements and support implementation.

● Strong commercial acumen and experience contributing to complex sales pursuits, RFP/RFI responses, solution proposals, executive presentations and deal conversion.

● Excellent communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to engage CXOs, business leaders, operations teams and technology stakeholders.

● Experience in banking technology, fintech or financial-services transformation is strongly preferred. Familiarity with agile product development and APIs/integrations is an advantage.

● Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent post-graduate qualification preferred.

**Why This Role**

You will work at the intersection of banking domain expertise, process transformation and technology—helping financial institutions solve real business problems while shaping the evolution of Intellect’s Trade Finance solutions.

The role offers direct customer exposure and the opportunity to influence solution design, product enhancements, sales outcomes and successful delivery.

This role is for a Trade Finance leader who combines deep domain expertise with hands-on technology and process experience. You will shape solution propositions for banks, actively demonstrate Intellect’s Trade Finance capabilities, and work closely with Engineering and Delivery to evolve the solution in response to market needs and client requirements. The role spans consultative engagement, product solutioning, sales support, and ongoing product

development—not just domain advisory or relationship management.

You will engage business, product, operations, and technology leaders to understand their objectives, diagnose process and business challenges, and translate them into practical, differentiated solutions. You should be equally comfortable leading a client workshop, running a product demonstration, developing a solution approach, and working with internal teams on the changes needed to deliver it.

**Role Definition**

The Vice President – Trade Finance Solutions owns domain-led solutioning and supports growth across Intellect’s Trade Finance portfolio. The role combines customer discovery, process analysis and reengineering, product demonstrations, solution design, bid support, and collaboration with Product, Engineering and Delivery to ensure that proposed solutions are credible, differentiated, feasible, and aligned with customer needs.

Prospect Understanding and Process Reengineering: Engage bank and financial-institution executives, business heads, product owners, operations and technology leaders to understand business models, workflows, pain points and strategic priorities. Finance solution across the trade lifecycle, solution walkthroughs, discovery workshops, use-case discussions, proof-of-concept sessions and technical/business presentations. ● 4. Solution Design and Proposal Development: Develop customer-specific solution approaches, scope documents, functional solution notes, implementation considerations, effort-estimation inputs, assumptions, exclusions and proposal content. ● 5. RFP/RFI and Deal Support: Lead or contribute to RFPs, RFIs, questionnaires, bid responses and presentations. Work with Sales and Pre-sales teams to qualify opportunities, articulate value propositions, address objections and support deal progression and closure.

Participate in solution reviews and relevant agile ceremonies; help ensure that requirements and acceptance criteria are clear and that changes address the underlying business need.

● 7. Delivery and Implementation Collaboration: Partner with Delivery, Implementation and Support teams to validate feasibility, integrations, dependencies, customization needs, effort assumptions and delivery risks. Support transition from sales to delivery and help resolve domain or solution issues during implementation where required.

● 8. Market and Customer Feedback Loop: Capture feedback from prospects, clients, demonstrations, implementations and competitive situations. Convert insights into actionable recommendations for product enhancements, roadmap priorities, solution assets and market positioning.

● 9. Commercial and Market Development: Support new sales, cross-sell and upsell across new and existing accounts. Engage senior stakeholders, contribute to pipeline development, and build trusted-advisor relationships

by connecting domain knowledge and technology capabilities to measurable business outcomes.

Product and Delivery teams through knowledge sharing and product training.

● 11. Innovation and Industry Awareness: Track market, regulatory and technology developments relevant to Trade Finance, including opportunities to apply AI and automation. Recommend practical enhancements and differentiated capabilities based on client needs and competitive trends.
